originalTitle: Kansai Nerolac Q1 profit rises 5%; approves Rs 601 crore capacity expansion
simplifiedContent: Kansai Nerolac, a company that makes paint, had a 5% increase in profit in the first quarter. This means they made more money than they did during the same time last year. The company says that people are still buying their products, even with problems happening around the world, which is good news for their business. They also plan to spend Rs 601 crore to expand their production, which should help them make even more paint in the future. The company is hopeful that the upcoming festive season will help their business continue to grow.

originalTitle: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Tuesday
simplifiedContent: Here's what happened in the stock market: Indian stocks went up a lot because the price of oil went down after the US and Iran started talking again. This made investors feel more positive, and as a result, the main stock market indexes (Sensex and Nifty) increased in value. The Sensex went up by 544 points and the Nifty by 1.6%, which added a huge amount of money (Rs 5 lakh crore) to the market. This increase was also helped by foreign investors putting more money into the market, the rupee getting stronger, and companies reporting good earnings. Overall, it was a good day for the stock market.

originalTitle: LIC OFS opens on August 4 as govt looks to sell up to 6.5% stake. Check details
simplifiedContent: The Indian government is selling some of its shares in the Life Insurance Corporation (LIC) to investors. This sale, called an "offer for sale", starts on August 4 for large investors and on August 5 for smaller, individual investors like you. The government plans to sell up to 6.5% of its shares in LIC. This sale is happening because the government wants to make sure that a certain percentage of LIC's shares are owned by the public, not just the government. By selling these shares, the government is following rules that require companies to have a minimum amount of public ownership.

originalTitle: New closing auction sparks rare Nifty-Sensex split amid low participation
simplifiedContent: Something unusual happened in the stock market recently. The Nifty and Sensex, which are two important market indexes, did something they rarely do - they moved in different directions at the end of the trading day. This happened because of a new way of closing trades, and some brokers think it was just a one-time mistake, while others believe it was because not many people understood the new system, causing an imbalance in buyers and sellers. The Nifty index suddenly jumped 200 points in just two minutes, which is a big move. This event is noteworthy because it shows that changes in the market's rules can have unexpected effects on stock prices.

originalTitle: Elevation plans twin stake sales in Paytm, Meesho after June-quarter earnings
simplifiedContent: Some investment companies, including Saif Partners and Elevation Capital, are planning to sell some of their shares in Paytm, a company listed on the stock market. They want to sell up to 14.9 million shares, which is about 2.3% of the total shares in Paytm. This sale will happen after Paytm announces its earnings for the quarter ending in June. This matters because it could affect the price of Paytm's shares, and it shows that some big investors are choosing to sell their stakes in the company. The sale is a notable event for Paytm and its shareholders, as it could impact the company's stock price.

originalTitle: SBI Funds Q1 Results: PAT rises 3% YoY to  ₹873 crore in first earnings after listing
simplifiedContent: SBI Funds Management, a company that manages investments, recently reported its financial results for the first quarter of the year. The company made a profit of ₹873 crore, which is 3.3% more than it made last year. This is a positive sign, especially since the overall market mood was not very strong. The company also saw an increase in the amount of money it manages, reaching ₹12.6 trillion, which is good news for the company and its investors. This growth was driven by individual investors putting their money into equity investments, showing that they still have confidence in the company.
